2607.07508.title: Single-Rollout Asynchronous Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
2607.07508.method: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07508v1#S3.SS1 — direct two-sided importance correction; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07508v1#S3.SS2 — trust mask and single-rollout critic; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07508v1#S4 — asynchronous actor/learner pipeline and update protocol
2607.07508.evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07508v1#S5 — agentic math/SWE tasks and throughput; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07508v1#S6 — algorithm ablations
2607.07508.limitations: arXiv:2607.07508v1#A2 — critic/rollout-cost assumptions, task scope and asynchronous staleness limits
2607.07508.artifact: Not Disclosed — exact v1 provides no source locator for artifact; No official public repository or uniquely versioned event-time artifact is disclosed in exact v1.
2607.07508.delta: SAO uses one rollout per prompt, trains a value critic more frequently than the actor and corrects current-policy learning directly against the rollout policy. Tokens whose two-sided importance ratio leaves a trust interval are masked rather than allowed to dominate. This trades group-relative variance reduction for lower rollout cost and explicit staleness control.
2607.07508.source_claim: Exact v1 supports the single-rollout/critic and direct importance-correction design plus bounded task gains. It does not establish universal sample-efficiency gains or production correctness under arbitrary actor lag.
2607.07508.analysis_old: Ch32 already owns the critic-stability branch; Ch33 already states rollout-policy identity, bounded freshness and one-rollout/asynchronous alternatives with explicit off-policy correction.
2607.07508.analysis_tradeoff: The method depends on critic quality, behavior-probability integrity and bounded staleness. It does not eliminate off-policy failure or prove one rollout is sufficient for arbitrary sparse-reward agents.

2607.07702.delta: STRACE converts noisy agent trajectories into typed dependency graphs, then slices backward from a failed outcome to isolate the minimal relevant action/observation chain and propose root-cause candidates. 2607.07953.method: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07953v1#S2 — unified recurrent notation across linear-attention families; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07953v1#S3 — CLER cross-layer routing; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07953v1#S4 — CLVR representation alignment

2607.07953.delta: A common recurrent form exposes where DeltaNet/GDN/Kimi-like architectures differ in decay, update and gating rather than treating names as incomparable systems. 2607.07953.analysis_tradeoff: Architecture rankings change with optimizer, learning rate and hybrid stack. CLVR gains diminish at scale and no serving benchmark proves runtime advantage.

2607.07964.title: KronQ: LLM Quantization via Kronecker-Factored Hessian
2607.07964.method: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07964v1#S3 — Kronecker-factored Hessian and bidirectional incoherence; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07964v1#S4 — Hessian-trace mixed precision

2607.07964.delta: KronQ approximates second-order weight sensitivity as output-gradient covariance Kronecker activation covariance, then uses two-sided incoherence transforms and Hessian-trace sensitivity for mixed-bit allocation. 2607.07964.analysis_tradeoff: The 70B BF16-versus-W4 hardware count is not apples-to-apples. Calibration adds roughly 8-11 seconds per layer and temporary H_G memory, and accuracy gains do not guarantee serving speed.

2607.08116.delta: Split a reasoning process into device-side prelude/coda and server-side recurrent reasoning units, then jointly route semantic work and wireless/compute resources rather than treating network placement as a fixed model split.
2607.08116.source_claim: Split a reasoning process into device-side prelude/coda and server-side recurrent reasoning units, then jointly route semantic work and wireless/compute resources rather than treating network placement as a fixed model split.
2607.08116.analysis_old: All-local inference preserves privacy and availability but is compute/energy bound; full remote serving is operationally simple but pays radio latency, connectivity and disclosure cost. Iterative reasoning makes this placement decision recur across latent steps.

2607.08716.title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
2607.08716.method: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08716v1#S3 — two-phase bank management and selective intervention
2607.08716.evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08716v1#S4 — Terminal-Bench 2.0 and tau2-Bench; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08716v1#S4.SS3 — full bank, advisor-only and always-on intervention controls
2607.08716.limitations: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08716v1#S5 — conclusion and bounded evidence; benchmark scope, memory authority and false-reminder risk remain open
2607.08716.delta: Separate memory maintenance from intervention: a memory agent turns trajectory evidence into a structured bank, then owns the control decision to remain silent or inject a concise, grounded reminder when future failure risk justifies Context cost.
2607.08716.source_claim: Separate memory maintenance from intervention: a memory agent turns trajectory evidence into a structured bank, then owns the control decision to remain silent or inject a concise, grounded reminder when future failure risk justifies Context cost.
2607.08716.analysis_old: Passive retrieval is reasonable when the acting agent knows when to ask. Long-horizon tasks fail when relevant evidence is not queried at the right step; exposing the whole bank or an always-on advisor avoids misses but adds distraction and unsupported advice.
2607.08716.analysis_tradeoff: Selective intervention reduces persistent Context pressure and can preempt repeated mistakes, but adds a learned control policy that can interrupt too often, stay silent at critical points, or generate reminders not grounded in authoritative memory. Bank provenance, reminder citation, abstention and intervention-cost metrics are required; passive retrieval remains preferable for short or deterministic workflows.

2607.08930.title: BlockServe: Block-Grained Continuous Batching for High-Throughput Diffusion LLM Serving
2607.08930.method: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08930v1#S2 — block-cycle scheduling, mixed-state layout and token-budget admission
2607.08930.evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08930v1#S3 — two diffusion LMs, four benchmarks and baseline comparison; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08930v1#S3.SS6 — block length and prompt sorting
2607.08930.limitations: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08930v1#S5 — evidence is limited to offline batching; online arrivals remain future work
2607.08930.artifact: Not Disclosed — exact v1 provides no source locator for artifact; No author repository or immutable implementation linked in exact v1
2607.08930.delta: Change the continuous-batching quantum from an autoregressive token iteration to a diffusion block-denoise cycle. Reclaim completed block slots immediately, align requests at heterogeneous denoising states in one dense layout, and admit work under a token/memory bounding box.
2607.08930.source_claim: Change the continuous-batching quantum from an autoregressive token iteration to a diffusion block-denoise cycle. Reclaim completed block slots immediately, align requests at heterogeneous denoising states in one dense layout, and admit work under a token/memory bounding box.
2607.08930.analysis_old: Static batching and token-level iteration scheduling are reasonable for synchronized forward calls or autoregressive decode. Diffusion LMs repeatedly refine blocks, and requests converge at different block boundaries, creating stragglers and heterogeneous mutable state that token-level scheduling cannot represent.
2607.08930.analysis_tradeoff: Finer blocks improve reclamation but add scheduling/denoising overhead; larger blocks improve efficiency but can amplify parallel-decoding approximation and reduce quality. Mixed-state layouts and token budgets add metadata/kernel complexity. Offline batches on one H200 do not establish online tail latency, arrival fairness or multi-GPU behavior; AR iteration scheduling remains right for AR models.

2607.08973.title: SiFAR: Synchronization-Free All-Reduce for Low-Latency LLM Inference
2607.08973.method: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08973v1#S3 — dual buffering and redundant pull; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08973v1#S4 — speculate, verify and retry collective protocol
2607.08973.evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08973v1#S5 — microbenchmarks and Megakernel end-to-end results; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08973v1#S6 — component analysis; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08973v1#S8.SS1 — sensitivity analysis
2607.08973.limitations: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08973v1#S9 — H200/NVSwitch, small-payload low-batch and Megakernel scope boundaries
2607.08973.artifact: Not Disclosed — exact v1 provides no source locator for artifact; No author repository linked; cited TensorRT-LLM/NCCL/DeepEP are references, not SiFAR implementation evidence
2607.08973.delta: For small-payload low-batch TP decode, remove the bottom barrier with dual buffers, reduce transfer with switch-assisted redundant pull, and replace the top readiness barrier with speculative fetch plus a reduced validation flag; retry on mis-speculation before committing the collective result.
2607.08973.source_claim: For small-payload low-batch TP decode, remove the bottom barrier with dual buffers, reduce transfer with switch-assisted redundant pull, and replace the top readiness barrier with speculative fetch plus a reduced validation flag; retry on mis-speculation before committing the collective result.
2607.08973.analysis_old: Oneshot/twoshot barriers and communication-compute overlap are reasonable at larger batches where compute hides communication. Latency-sensitive reasoning/agent decode minimizes batching; there is too little compute to hide collectives and barrier time dominates small payloads.
2607.08973.analysis_tradeoff: Speculation avoids flag exchange when ranks progress nearly together, but needs extra buffers, validation state and a retry path; imbalance raises retries. Switch reduction and Megakernel integration bind portability to topology/runtime. Correctness depends on buffer generation and validation ordering, not merely matching final tokens; conventional collectives remain safer on unsupported fabrics or larger/asynchronous workloads.

2607.09153.title: KV-PRM: Efficient Process Reward Modeling via KV-Cache Transfer for Multi-Agent Test-Time Scaling
2607.09153.method: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#S3.SS1 — representation-capacity argument; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#S3.SS2 — readout argument; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#A1.SS1 — assumptions; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#A1.SS2 — proof details; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#A1.SS3 — low-rank reward boundary; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#S4.SS1 — single verify-token readout over generation KV; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#S4.SS2 — LoRA-trained reward head and scoring flow; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#A2.SS1 — training implementation; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#A2.SS2 — verify-token implementation
2607.09153.evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#S5.SS1 — task and search protocol; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#S5.SS2 — accuracy comparisons; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#S5.SS3 — smaller text verifier and verify-token-count controls; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#S5.F3 — GH200 latency and memory measurement; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#S6 — KV Steering proof of concept; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#A3 — steering appendix
2607.09153.limitations: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#S8 — same-architecture requirement, theoretical assumptions and preliminary steering
2607.09153.artifact: Not Disclosed — exact v1 provides no source locator for artifact; No author repository or immutable event-time code artifact is linked in exact v1; RLHFlow/RLHF-Reward-Modeling is a cited baseline, not KV-PRM provenance
2607.09153.delta: Keep the generator's exact KV cache alive at the scoring boundary, switch to a compatible LoRA verifier adapter, append one verify token, attend that query over the existing K/V, and map the next-token logits for '+' and '-' to a process score. The readout advances only a query token rather than re-running a length-L prefill. The paper also explores differentiating through KV for steering, but that branch is preliminary and must not be merged with the verified read-only scoring mechanism.
2607.09153.source_claim: Keep the generator's exact KV cache alive at the scoring boundary, switch to a compatible LoRA verifier adapter, append one verify token, attend that query over the existing K/V, and map the next-token logits for '+' and '-' to a process score. The readout advances only a query token rather than re-running a length-L prefill. The paper also explores differentiating through KV for steering, but that branch is preliminary and must not be merged with the verified read-only scoring mechanism.
2607.09153.analysis_old: An independent text verifier is a sound default because it has a portable text interface, can use a different model and does not depend on ephemeral generator state. It becomes expensive when long trajectories are scored many times and the generator has already materialized the same prefix as KV state.
2607.09153.analysis_tradeoff: Representation reuse removes redundant prefill and can retain information not recoverable from decoded tokens, but couples verifier deployment to the generator architecture/state format and extends KV lifetime, memory pressure and access scope. Stale/mismatched KV may produce fluent scores rather than crashes. A reward readout can be miscalibrated or share the generator's blind spots; theoretical richness under assumptions does not prove causal correctness. Steering mutates latent state without a human-readable handoff and can reward-hack the PRM. Independent text verifiers remain preferable across heterogeneous models, remote trust domains, discarded caches, unsupported layouts or high-risk independent review.

2607.10183.title: Automated Tensor Scheduling for Hybrid CPU-GPU LLM Inference on Consumer Devices
2607.10183.artifact: Not Disclosed — exact v1 provides no source locator for artifact; No author repository is linked in exact v1; llama.cpp and Hugging Face Accelerate are cited dependencies, not ATSInfer provenance
2607.10183.delta: Profile per-tensor CPU/GPU execution and transfer costs, solve a memory-constrained static placement using measured performance density, keep nonresident tensors in pinned host memory, overlap Copy-Engine and SM-driven Zero-Copy transfers with computation, then observe realized transfer/compute time and re-run dynamic placement only after deviation and rate-limit thresholds are crossed. Prefill and decode retain distinct plans because their compute/memory balance differs.
2607.10183.source_claim: Profile per-tensor CPU/GPU execution and transfer costs, solve a memory-constrained static placement using measured performance density, keep nonresident tensors in pinned host memory, overlap Copy-Engine and SM-driven Zero-Copy transfers with computation, then observe realized transfer/compute time and re-run dynamic placement only after deviation and rate-limit thresholds are crossed. Prefill and decode retain distinct plans because their compute/memory balance differs.
2607.10183.analysis_old: Layer-level static offload is simple, predictable and amortizes profiling when the machine is dedicated and operator behavior is homogeneous. It becomes wasteful when tensors have different CPU/GPU speedup per byte and when local CPU, GPU or PCIe availability changes while prefill and decode share one device.
2607.10183.analysis_tradeoff: Tensor granularity improves use of scarce GPU bytes and runtime load feedback avoids a stale plan, but adds profiling, pinned memory, buffer reservation, graph rebuild, dynamic-program and hysteresis policy. Re-scheduling too often costs a material fraction of TPOT; too slowly leaves a stale plan. Thermal drift, unsupported kernels/formats, PCIe contention and inaccurate profiles can erase gains. Static layer placement remains preferable for stable dedicated hosts, small models, strict predictability or insufficient telemetry.

2607.10186.title: FlashAccel: Leveraging High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) for High-Throughput LLM Inference
2607.10186.artifact: Not Disclosed — exact v1 provides no source locator for artifact; No FlashAccel implementation or simulator repository linked in exact v1; cited GitHub pages are dependency/background sources
2607.10186.delta: Co-design an HBF stack and GPU attachment, distribute small SRAM buffers close to flash planes, map weights and KV into layouts that expose plane-level parallelism, prefetch future pages without stalling dependent kernels, and use an HBF-aware storage/programming layer to coordinate persistent and HBM/SRAM state. Capacity permits larger SLO-bounded batches; bandwidth and page latency remain the limiting constraints.
2607.10186.source_claim: Co-design an HBF stack and GPU attachment, distribute small SRAM buffers close to flash planes, map weights and KV into layouts that expose plane-level parallelism, prefetch future pages without stalling dependent kernels, and use an HBF-aware storage/programming layer to coordinate persistent and HBM/SRAM state. Capacity permits larger SLO-bounded batches; bandwidth and page latency remain the limiting constraints.
2607.10186.analysis_old: HBM-only residency gives the simplest latency and consistency contract; host/NVMe offload is cheaper and deployable but often exposes a slow transfer boundary. The constraint changes when flash can be integrated at HBM-like aggregate bandwidth and its latency hidden by die-level parallelism, SRAM prefetch and layout-aware scheduling.
2607.10186.analysis_tradeoff: The design exchanges new die/packaging area, SRAM, controller complexity, specialized layouts, simulator uncertainty, endurance/write amplification and heterogeneous fault recovery for much higher resident capacity. Strict SLOs can make lower-bandwidth configurations underperform HBM; hot mutable state may be a poor flash fit. HBM remains appropriate for hot latency-critical state, while conventional host/storage tiers remain preferable when new hardware is unavailable or persistence writes dominate.

2607.11942.title: How Query Visibility Changes KV-Cache Compression Rankings: A Matched-Budget Audit
2607.11942.artifact: https://github.com/NVIDIA/kvpress (audited upstream implementation, version 0.5.4); no immutable author harness/records locator is linked in exact v1 HTML
2607.11942.delta: Freeze identical models, instances, compression budgets and decoding; vary only whether the query is visible at compression time; compare each method against several trivial start/recent baselines with paired bootstrap; keep the attention backend fixed; run uncompressed and backend controls; quarantine tokenizer-invalid rows; withdraw rankings whose method requires a backend with a measured effect larger than method gaps.
2607.11942.source_claim: Freeze identical models, instances, compression budgets and decoding; vary only whether the query is visible at compression time; compare each method against several trivial start/recent baselines with paired bootstrap; keep the attention backend fixed; run uncompressed and backend controls; quarantine tokenizer-invalid rows; withdraw rankings whose method requires a backend with a measured effect larger than method gaps.
2607.11942.analysis_old: Query-aware compression is valid when each request owns a one-shot prompt and query, because the query is available to select relevant KV. It is invalid as evidence for shared/reusable cache compression, whose state must commit before downstream queries arrive. A benchmark label such as 8192 also ceases to be comparable when tokenizer expansion exceeds a model's positional budget.
2607.11942.analysis_tradeoff: Matched deployment protocols improve external validity but can exclude methods incompatible with the common backend or single-pass harness. Trivial baselines prevent false novelty but do not prove the winner is optimal. Backend numerical divergence, tokenizer overflow, OOM refill, lineage similarity and uniform ratios can silently reshape rankings. Query-aware evaluation remains appropriate for nonreusable per-query caches; query-agnostic evaluation is required for reusable caches.

2607.10350.title: ABot-AgentOS: A General Robotic Agent OS with Lifelong Multi-modal Memory
2607.10350.artifact: https://amap-cvlab.github.io/ABot-AgentOS (author project page; v1 states complete benchmark release is future work and private data/production results are not released)
2607.10350.delta: Insert a deliberative harness above low-level controllers; isolate skill contexts; maintain structured task state; verify stage and terminal conditions; store multimodal observations/traces as typed provenance-bound graph memory; diagnose failures after evaluation and promote derived evo-assets only to later splits. Edge/cloud separation attempts to keep private memory local while sharing common knowledge.
2607.10350.source_claim: Insert a deliberative harness above low-level controllers; isolate skill contexts; maintain structured task state; verify stage and terminal conditions; store multimodal observations/traces as typed provenance-bound graph memory; diagnose failures after evaluation and promote derived evo-assets only to later splits. Edge/cloud separation attempts to keep private memory local while sharing common knowledge.
2607.10350.analysis_old: A single controller and prompt-local memory are reasonable for short tasks and one embodiment. Long trajectories, dynamic events and repeated interaction create context drift, premature termination and untraceable updates; directly coupling reasoning to low-level control also makes hardware transfer expensive.
2607.10350.analysis_tradeoff: Hierarchy and persistent memory improve auditability and recovery but add skill-interface drift, verifier error, cross-store synchronization, privacy/access control and stale derived assets. Benchmark feedback can become leakage without split-order enforcement. The reported real-world/benchmark scope remains limited; noisy perception, actuation, network latency, safety and heterogeneous embodiments are not closed. A monolithic controller remains simpler for short, reversible, well-observed tasks.

2607.10463.title: GRASP: GRanularity-Aware Search Policy for Agentic RAG
2607.10463.artifact: Not Disclosed — exact v1 provides no source locator for artifact; No author repository/checkpoint linked in exact v1; Search-R1 Hugging Face collection is a baseline artifact, not GRASP provenance
2607.10463.delta: Expose semantic-search, keyword-search and read-parent-paragraph actions. Return sentence-level hits with parent metadata, let the policy expand a selected clue, and train a GRPO policy with answer, grounded-reading, complementary-search and turn-efficiency rewards. Retrieval observations are masked out of the policy loss; the model learns an explore/exact-match/verify sequence rather than a fixed fusion rule.
2607.10463.source_claim: Expose semantic-search, keyword-search and read-parent-paragraph actions. Return sentence-level hits with parent metadata, let the policy expand a selected clue, and train a GRPO policy with answer, grounded-reading, complementary-search and turn-efficiency rewards. Retrieval observations are masked out of the policy loss; the model learns an explore/exact-match/verify sequence rather than a fixed fusion rule.
2607.10463.analysis_old: A fixed dense or lexical top-k retriever is inexpensive, reproducible and effective for homogeneous short QA. Multi-hop problems change the state: different reasoning stages need different matching signals, and sentence-level discovery may need a later paragraph dereference rather than immediate full-context packing.
2607.10463.analysis_tradeoff: Adaptive tools and granularity can reduce irrelevant context and improve recall, but add tool calls, RL cost, reward shaping and premature-stop risk. Gold supporting facts make the reward nonportable; complementary-search rewards can encourage both tools even when one suffices. The result is shown on one 3B backbone and multi-hop QA corpora, not arbitrary enterprise RAG. Static hybrid retrieval remains preferable for low-latency or shallow tasks.

2607.10582.title: MemDecay: Region-Aware KV Cache Eviction for Efficient LLM Agent Inference
2607.10582.method: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10582v1#S3.SS2 — structural priors; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10582v1#S3.SS3 — calibrated region decay and attention refresh; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10582v1#S3.SS4 — page-granularity eviction; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10582v1#S3.SS5 — scope and tiered extension
2607.10582.evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10582v1#S4.SS1 — setup; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10582v1#S4.SS2 — lifetime measurement; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10582v1#S4.SS3 — budgeted recall; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10582v1#S4.SS4 — sensitivity and overhead
2607.10582.limitations: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10582v1#S5 — discussion, negative results and limitations
2607.10582.delta: An Agent orchestrator supplies typed semantic region labels and explicit pinning policy; the inference runtime combines those priors with calibrated decay and observed attention to make page-level KV eviction decisions.
2607.10582.source_claim: The paper supports region-dependent attention lifetimes, interpretable pinned retention and its synthetic budgeted-recall/overhead results. It also reports that the unnormalized attention term was much smaller than the structural term and that accumulated-attention retention beat MemDecay on unpinned recall at larger scale. It does not prove production long-context Agent quality or tail-SLO gains.
2607.10582.analysis_old: FullKV is the correctness baseline; recency/window and accumulated-attention policies are simpler when semantic labels are unavailable or unreliable. Agent traces change the constraint because the orchestrator already knows which spans are instructions, plans, tool outputs or scratch state.
2607.10582.analysis_tradeoff: Semantic labels and pinning make retention policy inspectable but convert orchestrator labeling errors into irreversible runtime deletion. Attention observation and eager-attention access add overhead; page means can dilute boundary regions; offload/recompute remain safer when future utility is uncertain.

2607.10599.title: MRUF: Multi-granularity Routing with Uncertainty-Aware Fusion for Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
2607.10599.method: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10599v1#S3.SS2 — modality-invariant alignment; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10599v1#S3.SS3 — multi-granularity routing and leave-one-out supervision; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10599v1#S3.SS4 — inverse-variance uncertainty-aware fusion; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10599v1#S3.SS5 — prediction and training objective
2607.10599.evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10599v1#S4.SS1 — datasets; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10599v1#S4.SS3 — implementation; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10599v1#S4.SS4 — efficiency; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10599v1#S4.SS6 — ablations; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10599v1#S4.SS7 — controlled perturbations; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10599v1#S4.SS8 — uncertainty/gate mechanism analysis
2607.10599.limitations: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10599v1#S4.SS7 — severe perturbation does not always improve MAE; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10599v1#S5 — training-cost and future-work boundary
2607.10599.artifact: Not Disclosed — exact v1 links no author repository, immutable implementation or checkpoint
2607.10599.delta: Separate task contribution from observation reliability: a contribution router is supervised by leave-one-out task degradation, while a distinct uncertainty head predicts modality-wise log variance and inverse-variance weights calibrate the final fusion gate.
2607.10599.source_claim: The source supports this mechanism and its MOSI/MOSEI author experiments, ablations and perturbation tests. Predicted uncertainty is a learned reliability sensor, not a probability that a modality is true, and the results do not establish broad multimodal robustness or production behavior.
2607.10599.analysis_old: Static, symmetric or task-contribution-only fusion is reasonable when modality quality is stable. Once occlusion, noise, missing inputs or transcript error vary per utterance, contribution and current reliability become distinct control signals.
2607.10599.analysis_tradeoff: Leave-one-out supervision adds masked forwards during training; uncertainty calibration adds a learned sensor whose correlations and distribution shift can be wrong. Inference remains one forward pass in the paper, but severe perturbations did not always improve regression MAE. Static or single-modality branches remain preferable when inputs are reliable, training budget is tight or calibration evidence is weak.

2607.10709.method: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10709v1#S3.SS2 — threat model; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10709v1#S4.SS2 — direct and contextual privacy scoring; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10709v1#S4.SS3 — pairwise utility dependency; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10709v1#S4.SS4 — constrained sanitization; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10709v1#S4.SS5 — local restoration

2607.10709.artifact: Not Disclosed — exact v1 links no author implementation; the CodeAlpaca GitHub citation is a dataset source, not PromptGraph provenance
2607.10709.delta: Move prompt privacy from independent PII-span masking to a client-owned graph that estimates contextual attribute leakage and pairwise utility dependencies, selects a privacy/utility cut, sends opaque placeholders, and restores only exact consistency-checked identifiers locally.
2607.10709.source_claim: The paper supports this single-turn honest-but-curious design and its MedQA/SAMSum/CodeAlpaca author experiments. It does not prove Differential Privacy, anonymity, compliance, adaptive-attacker resistance or production latency, and it does not disclose the exact local estimator, hardware or precision.
2607.10709.analysis_old: Regex and NER masking remain correct for explicit structured identifiers and low latency. Learned independent-span policies become insufficient when non-sensitive cues jointly reveal an attribute or when masking destroys relations required by the downstream task.
2607.10709.analysis_tradeoff: Relation-aware selection improves the measured privacy/utility frontier but depends on local detectors, attribute estimators, reconstruction proxies and sparse graph coverage. Greedy selection is approximate, placeholders can alter model behavior, and restoration must fail closed rather than granting the cloud model authority over private state.

2607.12395.title: Ring-Zero: Scaling Zero RL to a Trillion Parameters for Emergent Reasoning
2607.12395.artifact: https://github.com/THUDM/slime (paper-linked dependency; no immutable Ring-Zero release established)
2607.12395.delta: The pipeline combines clipped importance sampling, training-engine numerator correction, KL control, mixed-precision safeguards and context-parallel communication optimization; staged self-distillation/RL and length-conditioned modes separate discovery, sharpening and adaptive inference depth.
2607.12395.source_claim: The pipeline combines clipped importance sampling, training-engine numerator correction, KL control, mixed-precision safeguards and context-parallel communication optimization; staged self-distillation/RL and length-conditioned modes separate discovery, sharpening and adaptive inference depth.
2607.12395.analysis_old: Small-model RLVR with fixed context and ordinary importance ratios is reasonable when engine mismatch and communication depth are small. At trillion-parameter scale, low-probability amplification magnifies floating-point disagreement and context parallelism becomes a critical-path bottleneck.
2607.12395.analysis_tradeoff: The design improves stability and sample efficiency but depends on costly large-scale infrastructure, math-verifiable rewards and proprietary 1T-model evidence. Joint length training produced negative transfer at the high mode, ultra-long high-quality data remained limiting, and 64K training context bounded the claim.

2607.15550.method: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15550v1#S3 :: instruction screening followed by pre-execution semantic consequence and functional-state prediction; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15550v1#S4 :: Qwen3-VL-based safety-augmented world model trained jointly for screening, next-state prediction and risk judgment
2607.15550.evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15550v1#S5.SS1 :: MobileSafetyBench on Qwen3-VL-8B, GPT-5.1 and Gemini-3.1 planners; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15550v1#S5.SS2 :: instruction screening; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15550v1#S5.SS3 :: MobileRisk action-onset detection; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15550v1#A2.SS2 :: SFT configuration
2607.15550.limitations: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15550v1#S5.SS5 :: benefits differ by planner/category and early refusal changes latency accounting; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15550v1#S6 :: remaining fine-grained misses and benign false positives; no independent adversarial evaluation, calibrated risk probability, deployment concurrency or tail-SLO is disclosed
2607.15550.artifact: Not Disclosed — arXiv v1 links public training datasets and baseline models but no SeerGuard code, checkpoint or event-time repository
2607.15550.delta: A mobile GUI action guard can move from intent-only filtering to a two-stage execution boundary: reject malicious instructions first, then predict each proposed action's semantic consequence before effect. The guard remains a fallible sensor; the executor still owns authorization and fail-closed policy.
2607.15550.source_claim: The authors report that a separate consequence-prediction model can reduce risk under their MobileSafetyBench/MobileRisk contracts while preserving planner utility; they do not prove complete attack coverage or calibrated safety.
2607.15550.analysis_old: Intent filters were reasonable when risk was visible in the request, but benign instructions can produce unsafe state transitions after several GUI actions.
2607.15550.analysis_tradeoff: Pre-execution simulation adds model latency, false positives, world-model blind spots and stale-screen risk; deterministic policy checks and explicit user confirmation remain necessary for irreversible actions.

2607.15593.method: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15593v1#S3 :: gateway as shared MCP control point for protocol adaptation, authentication/access control, deterministic hybrid tool discovery and session-aware routing; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15593v1#S4 :: Go/Wasm production implementation on Alibaba Cloud L7 infrastructure
2607.15593.evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15593v1#S6.SS1 :: production regions, 2-core/4-GB gateway pods, Xeon 8369B, 3,616-tool catalog and ToolBench; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15593v1#S6.SS2 :: selection/token/latency; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15593v1#S6.SS4 :: protocol and session-state overhead
2607.15593.limitations: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15593v1#S7 :: centralized session coordination becomes a latency/reliability bottleneck, weak-semantic queries need knowledge-cache support, connection lifetime and skew complicate scaling; results are one provider's deployment and do not establish a portable MCP standard implementation
2607.15593.artifact: Not Disclosed — the paper describes a deployed proprietary gateway; https://github.com/ravitemer/mcp-hub is cited related work, not this system's artifact
2607.15593.delta: Direct MCP client-to-server connectivity does not scale to heterogeneous transports, large tool catalogs, centralized policy and stateful failover. A gateway can own protocol translation, identity-bound visibility, deterministic retrieval and session placement, but the session identifier and routing state become correctness-critical distributed state.
2607.15593.source_claim: The deployment shows that retrieval before model selection and a shared gateway can support thousands of tools, while centralized session state dominates gateway cost at scale; this is provider-scoped evidence.
2607.15593.analysis_old: Direct connection remains simpler for a small stable tool set, stateless transports and a single trust domain.
2607.15593.analysis_tradeoff: A shared control point adds blast radius, credential delegation, body inspection, catalog freshness and session-store/owner-routing failure modes; direct connections and stateless requests remain valid below the scale threshold.

2607.15621.method: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15621v1#S3.SS1 :: 337M action expert reads frozen 7B backbone per-layer KV without modifying it; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15621v1#S3.SS2 :: staleness-augmented training; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15621v1#S3.SS3 :: mutable cache refreshed at 5 Hz while action expert runs at 20 Hz with explicit invalidation
2607.15621.evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15621v1#S4.SS1 :: LMDrive/CARLA setup and baselines; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15621v1#S4.SS3 :: closed-loop driving; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15621v1#S4.SS4 :: latency; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15621v1#S4.SS6 :: cache/staleness ablations
2607.15621.limitations: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15621v1#S3.SS3 :: bounded staleness only holds inside the trained K=4 refresh interval and cache must rebuild on instruction/episode/history changes; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.15621v1#S5 :: evaluation remains CARLA/LMDrive-scoped and real-road safety, jitter, sensor loss and intervention recovery are not established
2607.15621.artifact: Not Disclosed — no author code/checkpoint/repository is linked from arXiv v1
2607.15621.delta: A fast-slow VLA can treat slow semantic inference as versioned cached state and run a smaller control expert against fresh observations at a higher frequency. Correctness requires training on the same staleness envelope, exact cache identity and explicit invalidation rather than pretending every action sees a fresh backbone.
2607.15621.source_claim: The authors show that a 5-Hz backbone/20-Hz expert pipeline can preserve their closed-loop CARLA driving metrics while reducing per-tick compute; they do not prove safety under real sensors or staleness beyond the trained bound.
2607.15621.analysis_old: Synchronous full-model inference was reasonable when the model met the control deadline and every action needed a fresh globally consistent observation.
2607.15621.analysis_tradeoff: Async execution reduces critical-path latency but introduces stale scene state, cache/version races, invalidation cost and split failure ownership; the synchronous path remains the safety fallback.

2607.15898.delta: A world model can separate slowly changing semantic structure from fast pixel detail and let the coarse prediction condition fine rollout. 2607.22690.delta: Memory construction can be deferred until the query: retrieve a broad evidence superset, then construct a small query-specific view in bounded parallel windows. This preserves raw archive authority while making the constructed memory disposable, versioned and recoverable.

A safe page table must commit lower precision before freeing pages and restore pages before committing higher precision; planner identity and per-request quality policy become part of serving correctness.

2607.16184.analysis_tradeoff: Dynamic precision adds calibration drift, prompt-conditioned policy risk, CPU-GPU traffic, mixed-kernel complexity and precision-transition recovery; static weights remain safer for strict reproducibility.

2607.16473.limitations: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.16473v1#S5 :: fine-grained domains add area, synchronization and control complexity; simulator-based TPUv5p-spec energy results are not silicon measurements, while TPUv4 results are validation/projections rather than TPU production-energy measurements; strict SLO preservation is author-simulated
2607.16473.artifact: https://github.com/google-coral/coralnpu :: open-source NPU core used for functional prototype; no author eNPU patch/commit or event-time artifact is disclosed
2607.16473.delta: DVFS can move from chip-wide frequency to component-level control when tensor operators stress different NPU units. The compiler must co-schedule instructions and voltage/frequency domains under request slack; otherwise synchronization and transition cost erase the energy benefit.
2607.16473.source_claim: The authors report simulator-based energy savings with functional RTL support and bounded area overhead; they do not provide production silicon measurements.
2607.16473.analysis_old: Chip-wide DVFS was reasonable because one frequency domain simplified timing closure, control and performance predictability.
2607.16473.analysis_tradeoff: Component domains add area, clock/voltage crossings, search complexity and SLO sensitivity; global DVFS remains preferable when slack is small or operator bottlenecks are uniform.

2607.18631.title: Searching for Plans You Can Actually Build: A Realizability-Aware Full-Space Optimizer for MoE Training and Serving
2607.18631.artifact: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.18631v1#A1 — exact v1 states that the artifact release URL and license are pending; no public artifact is credited
2607.18631.delta: The search IR spans parallelism, schedule and kernels. A dry-run reuses the code emitter as the realizability predicate, launch probes catch memory/runtime gaps the static predicate misses, and measured realization overhead is priced back into the search rather than represented as a separate rule list.
2607.18631.source_claim: The exact v1 supports emitter-defined realizability, launch probing, realization-tax calibration, and bounded single-node measurements. It does not prove that dry-run buildability guarantees runtime feasibility or that the reported search quality generalizes to frontier multi-node deployments.
2607.18631.analysis_old: Analytical cost search is reasonable when compiler, framework and kernel capability are stable and modeled constraints describe the executable domain. Once plan space spans phases, hardware and emitters, the optimizer can rank plans the actual toolchain cannot build.
2607.18631.analysis_tradeoff: Emitter reuse reduces drift but binds search to emitter completeness. Launch probing costs hardware time and still samples a finite environment. Evidence is single-node and small-model relative to frontier deployments; the artifact URL was not released in v1.

2607.18722.title: Stale but Stable: Staleness-Adaptive Trust Regions for Stabilizing Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning
2607.18722.artifact: https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/GradLoc; https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/GradLoc/commit/0fdd859a5945a59f3531ded48bc5d6cfd8a15fd5 — event-time repository pointer exists, but this pre-paper commit does not establish that the paper-specific SAT implementation was public
2607.18722.delta: SAT derives a detached sampled log-ratio, computes a batch-relative high-tail quantile, and contracts only the sign-selected outward side of PPO's interval. It is a drop-in sampled-surrogate change: the adaptive interval is contained in PPO's, pull-back updates are unchanged, and the objective differs only in the newly clipped outward band.
2607.18722.source_claim: The exact v1 supports a sampled log-ratio risk proxy and outward-only, batch-quantile clip contraction in one asynchronous math-RL setup. It does not establish a full-distribution trust-region guarantee, universal stability, or artifact-complete reproducibility.
2607.18722.analysis_old: Fixed PPO/GRPO clipping is reasonable when rollout and update policies remain near each other. Decoupled rollout/training pools create heterogeneous realized mismatch inside one batch, so checkpoint lag alone no longer describes sample risk.
2607.18722.analysis_tradeoff: Batch quantiles add distribution dependence and may shift with length/domain mixture. Sampled log-ratios can be huge on low-probability actions without large mass movement; sequence ratios can cancel token mismatch. SAT controls the sampled surrogate, not an all-action trust region.

2607.18754.title: AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents
2607.18754.delta: Typed trace capture feeds a multi-turn debugger that narrows agent, step and failure class; the diagnosis is converted into a bounded repair and evaluated by a single rerun. Failure taxonomy and framework integrations are extensible surfaces rather than model truth.
2607.18754.source_claim: The exact v1 and event-time repository support a typed trace-diagnosis-rerun toolkit and bounded evaluations on Who&When and failed GAIA tasks. They do not prove causal attribution, safe autonomous repair, privacy adequacy, or robustness across agent frameworks.
2607.18754.analysis_old: Manual or fixed-rule debugging is reasonable for short deterministic workflows. Multi-turn agents spread the originating fault and downstream symptoms across tool, model and environment spans; a trace alone then cannot safely authorize a repair.
2607.18754.analysis_tradeoff: More trace detail adds privacy, cost and schema coupling. Debugger errors can misattribute downstream symptoms, and rerun success can arise from stochasticity. Evaluation is narrow and framework instrumentation can change behavior.

2607.19438.title: BaseRT: Advancing Best-in-Class LLM Inference with Apple M5 Neural Accelerators
2607.19438.delta: Metal 4 cooperative-tensor kernels cover dense/MoE GEMM, fused expert projections and prefill attention. Dispatch selects this path only for compute-bound shapes/phases and retains specialized SIMD/GEMV kernels for memory-bound decode or unsupported hardware.
2607.19438.source_claim: The exact v1 and event-time repository support a phase- and silicon-specific Apple M5 implementation case with pinned single-device comparisons. They do not establish multi-request, multi-device, tail-latency, portability, or general accelerator superiority.
2607.19438.analysis_old: A single portable backend remains reasonable when portability, maintenance and predictable coverage dominate. Prefill and low-batch decode expose different compute/memory bottlenecks on a particular silicon generation, making phase-specific kernels worthwhile only inside a matched workload contract.
2607.19438.analysis_tradeoff: Hand-written kernels increase maintenance and portability cost. Results are Metal/M5-specific, single-user and single-device; no continuous batching, multi-request decoding or tensor parallelism is tested.

2607.19058.title: Where Should Optimizer State Live? Tiered State Allocation for Memory-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Training
2607.19058.delta: SkewAdam keeps momentum plus factored variance for the dense backbone, factored variance without momentum for experts, and exact variance for the router. Parameter role becomes the state-allocation key; this is orthogonal to ZeRO sharding and state quantization.
2607.19058.source_claim: The exact v1 and event-time repository support role-aware optimizer-state allocation in one deliberately shallow MoE training regime. They do not establish a universal optimizer, large-scale distributed wall-clock gains, or general convergence across architectures and data.
2607.19058.analysis_old: Uniform Adam state is the clearest baseline when parameters have similar update statistics and memory fits. MoE separates dense backbone, sparsely activated experts and sensitive routers, so identical moment state can spend memory on statistics whose value differs by role.
2607.19058.analysis_tradeoff: Role-specific rules increase optimizer complexity and depend on gradient sparsity. Evidence is one architecture/data regime and mostly one seed; the shallow model concentrates expert parameters. Factored estimates may fail where covariance is not approximately separable.

2607.19490.title: Integrity of peer-to-peer distributed LLM inference under malicious nodes
2607.19490.artifact: Not Disclosed — exact v1 provides no public repository, code release, or immutable artifact locator
2607.19490.delta: The verifier interleaves indistinguishable known-answer canaries, stores clean fp32 intermediate activations, measures per-shard relative-L2 mismatch against live fp16 activations and ranks shards by per-canary AUROC rather than relying on one universal threshold.
2607.19490.source_claim: The exact v1 supports relative-L2 known-answer canaries as comparative integrity evidence in 408 simulated configurations. It does not establish production P2P integrity, heterogeneous-noise calibration, adaptive-attacker resistance, or authorization to evict a peer.
2607.19490.analysis_old: Artifact signatures and final-output checks are reasonable when execution stays inside trusted infrastructure. Pipeline-parallel inference across untrusted peers needs evidence at intermediate state boundaries because a wrong final token cannot localize the stage that corrupted it.
2607.19490.analysis_tradeoff: References require trusted precomputation and activation storage. Real heterogeneous nondeterminism is not isotropic Gaussian; models are small. Adaptive attackers can fingerprint canaries or tune below the measured floor, and persistent-on-every-query attacks are easier than selective attacks.

2607.22997.limitations: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.22997v1#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1 — the real-robot transfer evidence is qualitative and scoped to the described basic pick-and-place distribution; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.22997v1#S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1 — cross-device throughput is task/algorithm dependent and the text itself attributes results to unisolated host, synchronization and batch effects
2607.22997.artifact: https://github.com/AMD-AIM/Physical_AI_Challenge; https://github.com/PhysicalAI-AIM/Robot_synthetic_data_generation_workshop; https://github.com/ZJLi2013/vk-gsplat-plugin — exact v1 discloses these resources, but event-time immutable commits and an end-to-end reproduction were not audited, so no code-level or reproducibility claim is retained
2607.22997.delta: The paper composes Genesis simulation, LeRobot-format demonstrations, SmolVLA fine-tuning, 3DGS scene reconstruction, ROCm/PyTorch execution and physical Franka deployment into four demonstrations on AMD hardware. It is a portability and workflow-integration case, not a new VLA, sim-to-real, control, or scheduling mechanism.
2607.22997.source_claim: The exact v1 supports that the authors assembled and demonstrated the described AMD/ROCm workflows and disclosed resource links. It does not prove general sim-to-real robustness, safety, causal world-model correctness, matched cross-hardware superiority, or artifact-complete reproduction.
2607.22997.analysis_old: A heterogeneous simulator/training/deployment toolchain is reasonable when each phase uses the most mature backend and explicit interchange artifacts are maintained. A unified ROCm stack reduces translation and environment handoff cost, but the paper does not show that software-stack unification removes the semantic sim-to-real boundary.
2607.22997.analysis_tradeoff: A unified software stack lowers phase-boundary integration cost, but it can hide task-specific kernel maturity, driver/version coupling and host bottlenecks behind an end-to-end label. Photorealistic 3DGS backgrounds do not guarantee contact dynamics; synthetic success can fail under calibration, sensor, friction and latency shift. Vendor-authored cross-hardware throughput without matched controls cannot establish a general hardware ranking.

2607.23250.title: Libra: Taming Attention Workload Skew in Long-Context LLM Training with Bounded Sequence Pool
2607.23250.limitations: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.23250v1#S2.SS2 — the design is scoped to dense causal attention; sparse or linear attention is left to future work; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.23250v1#S5.p6 — raw-sample step semantics are preserved but bitwise-equivalent gradients, optimizer states and trajectories are explicitly not claimed; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.23250v1#S6.SS1 — WLB-LLM is reimplemented without outlier deferral and DistCA is scope-emulated rather than run end-to-end; PP bubble reduction is inferred from forward-time compression rather than a pipeline trace
2607.23250.artifact: Not Disclosed — exact v1 contains no public Libra code or artifact URL; the MagiAttention repository is a cited baseline resource, not the reviewed system's implementation
2607.23250.delta: Libra freezes the raw-sample multiset of each optimizer step, partitions its DP replicas into fixed-size sequence pools, uses exact-cardinality variance-reduced placement to pair complementary packed-sequence workloads across pools, then dispatches sequence-by-head tiles within each pool. A CPU planner emits per-iteration plans; the GPU executor performs planned Q/K/V and output all-to-all around an unmodified variable-length FlashAttention kernel, with chunked overlap. Scaling DP creates more pools rather than expanding the communication domain of each pool.
2607.23250.source_claim: The exact v1 supports that equal-token packing can leave dense-attention workload skew, and that a bounded sequence-pool design with step-preserving placement, sequence-head tiling and overlapped tensor exchange improved the stated Qwen3/NVIDIA workloads. It does not establish bitwise training equivalence, sparse/linear-attention applicability, complete end-to-end superiority over WLB-LLM or DistCA, public reproducibility, or topology-independent gains.
2607.23250.analysis_old: Fixed-token packing plus Ulysses is reasonable when token count approximates work and variation remains within each CP group. Long-tailed raw sequences break that approximation because attention work is quadratic within each constituent sequence, while cluster-wide disaggregation expands the communication and failure domain. The changed constraint is therefore not merely more GPUs, but the scope over which work may be redistributed without changing optimizer-step membership.
2607.23250.analysis_tradeoff: A bounded pool reduces global communication exposure and indivisible-outlier pressure, but adds all-to-all traffic, CPU planning, metadata broadcast, tile/KV bookkeeping and floating-point reordering. Pool size and tile shape are workload/topology dependent; overlap cannot hide first-dispatch/final-return costs, and adding more pools still grows the worst-pool tail. The evidence assumes microbatch size one, dense causal attention, proprietary production datasets and one NVIDIA NVLink/RoCE environment. Ordinary packing/Ulysses remains preferable when sequence skew is mild or orchestration cost dominates; a broader global pool may win inside a uniformly high-bandwidth domain.

2607.25884.title: CONQuER: Hardware-Aware Mixed-Precision Quantisation with Online-Calibrated Surrogates
2607.25884.delta: Direct Evolution: framework-side bit assignment -> compiler-visible quantization IR -> surrogate-prescreened search -> selective hardware calibration.
2607.25884.source_claim: Supports compiler-integrated, selectively measured MPQ search. It does not prove surrogate convergence, universal Pareto dominance or transfer of one policy across hardware/compiler versions.
2607.25884.analysis_old: Framework-side mixed precision and analytic latency proxies are cheap and portable, but compiler lowering can map the same bit-width policy to very different physical execution.
2607.25884.analysis_tradeoff: Hardware-in-loop calibration corrects analytic proxies but consumes compile/run budget and risks overfitting to one device/software stack. Static quantization remains simpler when the deployment target is fixed and well-characterized.
